title: Capacity Concierge: Quarterly roadmap for hedged reservations and gradual surge orchestration
creator: Sofia Martinez
description:
Summary:
This initiative establishes the 'Capacity Concierge' program: a quarterly roadmap slice to introduce hedged reservations and a gradual surge orchestration algorithm for Dedicated pools. The goal is to reduce overall unit cost while preserving latency SLOs by programmatically hedging short-term reservation commitments and slowly increasing prewarm capacity in response to predictive demand signals.

Objectives:
- Deliver a canaryable, policy-driven orchestration that blends reserved pools with elastic surge capacity.
- Implement a hedging strategy to cover short, high-percentile demand without long-duration reservations.
- Provide SLO-safe rollout paths (canary, percentage ramp, automatic fallback) and clear cost/latency telemetry.

What we'll build this quarter:
1) Hedged reservation allocator: algorithm and API to commit short-duration reservations automatically based on demand percentiles and cost forecast.
2) Gradual surge orchestration: controller that increments prewarm capacity in small steps with rapid rollback on degradation.
3) Canary rollout pipeline: route 10% of qualifying traffic through Capacity Concierge with observability hooks.
4) Cost/latency dashboard: per-route cost delta, utilization, and 99th-percentile latency for canary and baseline.

Success metrics (Q2 targets):
- Net unit cost reduction >= 12% on hedged workloads at P95+ demand months.
- Maintain 99th-percentile latency within 1.2x of baseline for canary traffic.
- False-positive surge rollbacks (unnecessary scaling) < 8% of surge events.
- Canary adoption: 10 production customers enrolled in pilot by end of quarter.

Trade-offs and considerations:
- Aggressive hedging reduces cost but raises risk of capacity debt if predictions are wrong. We will limit hedged reservation duration to 4 hours by default.
- Gradual surge prioritizes latency safety over cold-start cost savings; some short-lived bursts may still pay more tokens.
- Finance requires visibility into short-duration commits; we'll emit an hourly hedging ledger.

Rollout plan:
- Week 0-4: Algorithm design, simulation on historical telemetry, and finance sign-off on hedging rules.
- Week 5-8: Implement allocator service + orchestration controller; infra tests and staging runs.
- Week 9-10: Canary deployment (10% traffic) with tight SLO monitoring and automated rollback hooks.
- Week 11-12: Iteration, customer pilot enrollment, and post-mortem for broader rollout decision.

Risks and mitigations:
- Prediction model regressions: include shadow mode and gating by simulation confidence.
- Latency regressions during ramp: cap ramp velocity and require SLO pass to continue.
- Accounting complexity: produce a hedging ledger and reconcile with billing.

Related artifacts:
- Design doc (Confluence): https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ENG/pages/CC-Design
- Prototype runbook (Google Drive): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1CapacityConcierge
- Simulation notebooks (internal): https://git.redwood.ai/redwood/hedge-sims
- Dashboard (Looker): https://datastudio.redwood.ai/d/cc-canary-dashboard

Next steps:
- Finalize hedging parameters with Finance (cost tolerance, max hourly commits).
- Schedule cross-functional kickoff with Infra, SRE, and SDK teams.
- Prepare canary acceptance criteria and rollback playbook.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Hedged allocator prototype validates on four weeks of historical traffic with simulated cost delta <= target.
2) Gradual surge controller supports policy input (ramp delta, max capacity) and automated rollback on latency breach.
3) Canary pipeline can toggle routing to 10% and emit per-customer telemetry to the dashboard.
4) Finance has access to hourly hedging ledger and has signed off on short-duration reservation rules.
